h1: FPA in Electricity Bill: What It Means and How to Calculate It
title: FPA in Electricity Bill: Meaning & Latest Rate | Wattlyst
meta: What fuel price adjustment (FPA) means on your bill, the latest NEPRA-verified rate with the decision link, and how to calculate it yourself.
author: ali-ahmad

breadcrumb.name: FPA in Electricity Bill: What It Means and How to Calculate It

sections.h2: What is fuel price adjustment (FPA) on an electricity bill?
p: Every electricity tariff in Pakistan is built on a reference fuel cost: the price per unit that NEPRA assumed the power plants would pay for gas, coal, furnace oil and imported fuel when it set the tariff. The real cost moves every month with fuel prices, the exchange rate and how much hydro and solar power was available. The fuel price adjustment is the mechanism that passes the difference to consumers, one month at a time, under the NEPRA Act.

On the bill it appears as a single line, FPA or fuel adjustment, equal to the month's notified rate times the units billed. At the pre-filled July 2026 rate, 300 units carry Rs 617. GST is charged on the subtotal that includes it, so the real cost of the line is a little higher than the line itself.

sections.h2: How is the FPA calculated and who decides it?
p: The Central Power Purchasing Agency (CPPA-G) files a request with NEPRA after each month closes, showing the actual fuel cost of the generation bought that month against the reference. NEPRA advertises a public hearing, hears the request and objections, and issues a decision with a notification in the official Gazette. The decision names the month the adjustment belongs to and the month in which the DISCOs are to recover it, which is why the FPA on a September bill can refer to July's fuel.

The arithmetic is a subtraction: actual fuel cost per kWh minus reference fuel cost per kWh. If more expensive fuel ran in a month with poor hydro flows, the rate comes out positive; a month with cheap hydro and low oil prices gives a negative rate. The same rate applies to all ex-WAPDA DISCOs, and NEPRA applies it to K-Electric consumers too, under the Federal Government's policy guidelines for a uniform FCA, so a unit costs the same FPA in every company.

sections.h2: Positive and negative FPA: what each means for your bill
p: A positive FPA is an extra charge. The pre-filled rate on this page is the one NEPRA determined for July 2026, the latest FPA in the Bill Index, and on 300 units it adds Rs 617 before GST. A negative FPA is a credit of the same shape: NEPRA has in past months notified negative adjustments, and the second example below shows what a small negative rate does to the same bill.
Either way the effect scales with units. A home on 700 units pays or receives more than twice what a home on 300 units does, so the FPA matters most in the months when consumption is already highest.

l.t: latest FPA in the Bill Index

sections.h2: FPA vs FCA: is there a difference?
p: No. FPA (fuel price adjustment) and FCA (fuel charges adjustment) are two names for the same monthly line. NEPRA's decisions use fuel charges adjustment; most DISCO bills print FPA; K-Electric bills print FCA. Some bills also show it as fuel adjustment or F.P.A. with a month next to it, which is the month the fuel was burnt, not the month of the bill.

sections.h2: What is QTA in the electricity bill, and how is it different from FPA?
p: QTA is the quarterly tariff adjustment. It settles the non-fuel side of the tariff over a three-month period: capacity payments to power plants, transmission and distribution costs and similar items that do not move with the price of fuel. It too is determined by NEPRA and notified, and it too can be positive or negative. On this page it is a separate input under advanced settings, chosen by billing quarter, and it appears as its own line of Rs 156 on the default bill.

The practical difference: the FPA changes every month and tracks fuel; the QTA changes once a quarter and tracks everything else. Both are per unit, both are exempt for lifeline consumers, and both are added to the subtotal before GST.

sections.h2: Why is my bill high because of FPA, and who is exempt?
p: When a month with heavy AC use lands on a bill carrying a large positive FPA, the line can be the biggest surprise on the page: at the pre-filled rate a 700 unit month carries Rs 1,441 of FPA before GST. NEPRA's decision for the July 2026 adjustment (SRO 1499(I)/2026) charges the FPA to every consumer category except lifeline consumers, electric vehicle charging stations and prepaid consumers, so a protected home pays it too; check the next month's decision for any change to the list. Only the review decision for March 2026, a month with a small negative adjustment, also left out protected consumers.

If the FPA on your bill does not match the notified rate for that month times your units, or if a lifeline bill carries an FPA line, that is a billing error worth raising with the DISCO. An FPA line on a protected bill is normal. The overbilling check walks through the other common errors.

faq.q: What is the fuel adjustment this month?
faq.a: It is whatever NEPRA notified for the month whose fuel is being recovered on your bill. The rate pre-filled on this page is the latest NEPRA-verified one, the July 2026 adjustment charged on September 2026 bills. October 2026 bills carry Rs 1.11 per unit for August 2026, reported in the news; this page keeps the latest NEPRA-verified rate until that decision is published. Either way, check the NEPRA decision linked under sources and the FPA line on your own bill, and replace the rate here.

faq.q: How do I calculate FPA charges on my bill?
faq.a: Multiply the units on the bill by the FPA rate for the month: 300 units at the pre-filled rate give Rs 617. Then expect GST at 18% on the subtotal that includes it.

faq.q: What is FCA in an electricity bill?
faq.a: The same thing as FPA: fuel charges adjustment is NEPRA's and K-Electric's name for the monthly fuel price adjustment. NEPRA applies the same rate to K-Electric consumers as to the ex-WAPDA DISCOs, under the Federal Government's policy guidelines for a uniform FCA.

Yes. When the actual fuel cost for the month was below the reference cost in the tariff, NEPRA notifies a negative adjustment and the bill shows a credit. The second worked example shows a negative rate on 300 units.

Lifeline consumers, electric vehicle charging stations and prepaid consumers. NEPRA's July 2026 decision (para 21(a)) charges every other category, protected homes included; check each month's decision for any change to the list. The review decision for March 2026 also spared protected consumers, but only for that month.

faq.q: What is QTA in the electricity bill?
faq.a: The quarterly tariff adjustment, a per-unit line that settles capacity and other non-fuel costs over a three-month period. It is separate from the FPA, can also be positive or negative, and is chosen by billing quarter under advanced settings on this page.

faq.q: Why is my bill high this month because of FPA?
faq.a: A positive FPA is charged on every unit, so a high-use month with a large adjustment can add thousands of rupees: on 700 units the default rate adds Rs 1,441 before GST. If the line does not equal the notified rate times your units, query it with the DISCO.

faq.q: Why is my real bill higher than this estimate when it is over Rs 25,000?
faq.a: A bill of Rs 25,000 or more a month carries advance income tax under section 235 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001: 7.5% of the bill for a domestic consumer who is not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List. This calculator leaves it out because it depends on your tax status; check the income tax line on your bill and FBR's current withholding tax card.

key_facts: FPA, the fuel price adjustment (printed as FCA, fuel charges adjustment, on K-Electric and NEPRA documents), is a monthly per-unit figure that NEPRA determines after a public hearing and notifies in the Gazette; the DISCOs apply it to a later month's bills.
The FPA is positive when the actual fuel cost of generation was above the reference cost built into the tariff and negative when it was below: a negative FPA is a credit that lowers the bill.
FPA line = FPA rate × units: at NEPRA's July 2026 rate, a 300 unit bill carries Rs 617 of FPA, and GST at 18% is charged on it as well.

NEPRA's fuel adjustment orders charge the monthly FPA to every consumer category except lifeline consumers, electric vehicle charging stations and prepaid consumers (July 2026 decision, SRO 1499(I)/2026, para 21(a)), so protected homes pay it; the review decision for March 2026 (SRO 852(I)/2026) spared protected consumers for that one month only.
QTA is different: the quarterly tariff adjustment covers capacity and other non-fuel costs over a three-month period; the FPA covers fuel only and changes every month.

Income tax is not in this estimate: under section 235 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001, a home not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List pays advance income tax of 7.5% on a monthly bill of Rs 25,000 or more; consumers on the list pay none.
mistakes: Reading the FPA month as the bill month. The month printed next to the FPA is the month whose fuel is being adjusted; the charge lands on a later bill.
Treating the FPA as a fixed tax. It is a different number every month and can be a credit; copy the rate from each bill rather than carrying one over.
Forgetting GST on the FPA. GST at 18% is charged on the subtotal including the FPA line, so Rs 617 of FPA costs more than that.
Confusing FPA with QTA. The FPA is monthly and about fuel; the QTA is quarterly and about capacity and other costs. Both can appear on the same bill.

Disputing the FPA line on a protected bill. Protected homes pay the FPA; NEPRA spares only lifeline, EV charging station and prepaid consumers, so an FPA charge on a lifeline bill is the one to query with the DISCO.

fields.label: Sanctioned load
fields.hint: The kW printed on the bill. It sets the fixed charge, not the FPA. At 5 kW or more use the ToU bill calculator.

fields.hint: Tick if your bill shows the protected category. Protected homes pay the FPA too: NEPRA's fuel adjustment orders spare only lifeline, EV charging station and prepaid consumers.

fields.hint: Only for very small consumers whose bill shows the lifeline category; lifeline bills carry no FPA.

fields.label: Billing quarter for QTA
fields.hint: The quarterly tariff adjustment is a separate line from the FPA and depends on the quarter.

fields.name: fc_surcharge_per_unit

fields.hint: Financing cost surcharge per unit, from the bill. Secondary-source default.

fields.hint: Sales tax applied to the bill subtotal, FPA included.

content.answer: FPA (fuel price adjustment) is a per-unit charge or credit NEPRA sets monthly for the gap between tariff and actual fuel cost. October 2026 bills carry Rs 1.11 per unit for August 2026, reported in the news. FPA line = rate × units: at the pre-filled July 2026 rate (latest NEPRA-verified), 300 units add Rs 617, plus GST.

formula.text: FPA line = FPA rate (Rs per unit, notified by NEPRA for the month) × units billed; GST is then charged on the subtotal that includes it
lines: FPA rate = actual fuel cost per kWh of the month's generation − reference fuel cost per kWh in the tariff
positive rate = extra charge; negative rate = credit
not applied to lifeline, EV charging station and prepaid consumers (NEPRA); protected homes pay it
bill = energy + fixed + FC surcharge + QTA + FPA, then + GST
